oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The anchor of this essay is the poem by Ranier-Maria Rilke which Hans-Georg Gadamer positioned as the frontispiece of his major work, Warheit and Methode. My translation and exploration of the meaning of this poem offer consideration of the reasons Gadamer may have had for thus positioning Rilke's poem, giving attention to Gadamer's intellectual, professional, and personal relationship with Heidegger. Over the past sixty-four years, my own association with Gadamer and his work has brought me to further reflection on their friendship. Hence, the title of this essay, Hans-Georg Gadamer: Philosopher, Teacher, Friend. I offer here my English translation of the poem as my principal contribution to this essay. As a philosopher with theological leanings, I propose, second, to use Rilke’s poem to bring some clarity to the complex interplay of, Rilke’s, Gadamer’s, and Heidegger’s own “application” in their work on what is called a Kehre or “turn."
